title: Express Middleware
content: Express middleware functions execute before the route handler. They can modify the request object, response object, or end the request-response cycle.

title: Express Routing
content: Express routing determines how an application responds to a client request on a particular endpoint using methods such as GET, POST, PUT and DELETE.

title: REST API
content: A REST API follows the principles of Representational State Transfer and commonly uses HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.

title: JWT Authentication
content: JWT authentication is stateless because the server does not store session information. The client sends the token with every request.

title: Session Authentication
content: Session authentication is stateful because the server stores the session information and identifies the user using a session ID stored in cookies.

title: Cookies
content: Cookies are small pieces of data stored inside the browser and are automatically sent with every request to the same domain.

title: Socket.IO
content: Socket.IO enables real-time bidirectional communication between the client and the server using events such as emit and on.

title: Multer
content: Multer is an Express middleware used for handling multipart form-data and uploading files from the client.

title: Cloudinary
content: Cloudinary is a cloud-based media storage service used to upload, optimize and deliver images and videos.

title: MongoDB
content: MongoDB is a NoSQL document database that stores data as BSON documents instead of rows and columns.

title: Mongoose
content: Mongoose is an ODM library for MongoDB that provides schemas, models and validation for Node.js applications.

title: TypeScript
content: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that adds static typing, interfaces, enums, generics and compile-time error checking.

title: Generics
content: Generics allow reusable components to work with different data types while maintaining type safety.

title: Interfaces
content: Interfaces define the structure of objects and are commonly used to enforce contracts in TypeScript.

title: Docker
content: Docker packages an application along with its dependencies into containers so that it runs consistently across environments.
